stories.headline: Appeals court reduces former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's insurrection sentence to 15 years
stories.summary: The Seoul High Court on May 7 reduced former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's prison sentence from 23 years to 15 years for his role in ex-President Yoon Suk-yeol's December 2024 martial law declaration. The court upheld most convictions but cited Han's 50-plus years of public service and his comparatively limited role relative to Yoon as mitigating factors; it also found that even a proper Cabinet deliberation could not have stopped Yoon from proceeding.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea signals shift toward rate hikes as inflation rises on energy shock
stories.summary: Bank of Korea Senior Deputy Governor Ryoo Sang-dai said at the sidelines of the ADB annual meeting in Samarkand on May 4 that it is 'time to consider stopping rate cuts and thinking about increases,' with the next policy meeting set for May 28. Analysts at DBS and ING noted the BOK's shift toward hawkish guidance amid April inflation accelerating to a near two-year high of 2.6% year-on-year, driven largely by energy costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz closure.

stories.headline: June 3 local elections tighten as DPK landslide forecast fades and PPP recovers
stories.summary: What had appeared a near-certain landslide victory for the ruling Democratic Party of Korea in the June 3 local elections for mayors and governors is becoming more competitive, with conservative candidates narrowing gaps in multiple regions; polls show PPP recovery partly driven by backlash against the special counsel bill. The PPP warned against DPK 'parliamentary dictatorship' after the ruling party's floor leader Han Byung-do won reelection, and 1,325 PPP members in Daegu defected to endorse the DPK's Daegu mayoral candidate, adding complexity to the race.

stories.headline: Constitutional amendment bill collapses as PPP filibuster blocks first revision attempt in 39 years
stories.summary: The ruling DPK's bid to put a partial constitutional amendment to a national referendum concurrent with the June 3 local elections collapsed on May 8 when National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik suspended the process after the PPP announced it would filibuster all agenda items; the bill, co-sponsored by 187 lawmakers excluding the PPP, sought to toughen conditions for declaring martial law and enshrine democratic movement history in the preamble. The failed vote marks South Korea's first unsuccessful constitutional revision attempt in 39 years.

stories.headline: Samsung reaches $1 trillion market cap as KOSPI breaks 7,000 on AI chip demand
stories.summary: South Korea's KOSPI benchmark index surpassed 7,000 for the first time on May 6, driven by an AI-powered surge in semiconductor stocks, with Samsung Electronics crossing the $1 trillion market capitalization mark — the second Asian firm after TSMC to do so. The KOSPI continued setting all-time highs through May 8, closing just below 7,500; reports also emerged that Apple held exploratory talks with Samsung about manufacturing chips in the US.

stories.headline: DPK pushes special counsel bill on alleged fabricated prosecutions; PPP launches task force to block it
stories.summary: The ruling Democratic Party advanced legislation to establish an independent special counsel to review multiple criminal cases against President Lee Jae-myung that the DPK alleges were fabricated by prosecutors under the Yoon administration; a parliamentary special committee filed complaints against 31 individuals linked to the alleged fabrications. President Lee urged 'careful deliberation' and the DPK delayed the bill's final timing ahead of June 3 elections; the PPP announced a task force to block the legislation, calling it an attempt to withdraw prosecutions against Lee.

stories.headline: Samsung semiconductor workers reject $340,000 bonus offer, threaten 18-day strike over AI profit share
stories.summary: Workers in Samsung's semiconductor division rejected a management offer of approximately $340,000 per employee (roughly 13% of the chip division's operating profit as a one-time payment), demanding instead annual contractual payouts comparable to those at rival SK Hynix where workers stand to receive up to $900,000. The union announced a planned 18-day general strike from May 21 to June 7, which analysts warned could disrupt HBM chip production and affect AI supply chains; Samsung's consumer division union did not join the strike action.

stories.headline: NIS briefs lawmakers on North Korea's constitutional amendment mandating automatic nuclear strike if Kim Jong Un killed
stories.summary: South Korea's National Intelligence Service disclosed to senior officials that North Korea's Supreme People's Assembly adopted a constitutional amendment on March 22 mandating an automatic nuclear retaliation strike if Kim Jong Un is assassinated or incapacitated; the revision was publicly revealed in an NIS briefing to senior South Korean officials during the week of May 8. The change reportedly reflects Kim's concerns after observing how US and Israeli forces neutralized Iranian leadership.

stories.headline: Lee Jae-myung says people saved him from 2024 knife attack; civil rights commission overturns emergency airlift ruling
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung posted a message on May 9 saying the public saved him from what he called a 'terrorist murder attempt' in January 2024, a day after the state civil rights commission overturned an earlier ruling concerning his emergency airlift from Busan to Seoul following the stabbing attack. Lee pledged to devote himself entirely to the country; the commission's finding was related to whether the airlift involved preferential treatment.

stories.headline: KOSPI bull run drives debt-fueled investing surge, BOK study shows weak wealth-to-consumption link
stories.summary: As the KOSPI continued setting record highs through early May, a Bank of Korea study found that South Korean households spend only about 130 won per 10,000 won of stock gains—far below international norms—with profits typically flowing into real estate rather than consumption; separately, overdraft balances at the five largest banks reached their highest level in over three years as retail investors piled into leveraged stock positions, with investors in their 50s and 60s notably increasing their exposure.

stories.headline: South Korean vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz; probe launched, opposition demands government response
stories.summary: South Korea's Oceans Ministry launched a formal investigation on May 8 into an explosion and fire aboard a Korean-operated vessel (identified in later coverage as the HMM Namu) in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran-linked commentary suggesting the ship was targeted; Seoul kept all possibilities open pending fact-finding. A PPP lawmaker subsequently demanded President Lee respond to what the opposition characterized as the government downplaying a confirmed attack, raising questions about South Korea's posture on US-led maritime security missions.

stories.headline: South Korea's March current account surplus hits record $37.3 billion on semiconductor export boom
stories.summary: The Bank of Korea reported on May 8 that South Korea's current account surplus reached a record $37.33 billion in March, driven by a 149.8% year-on-year surge in semiconductor exports and a travel account surplus—the first in 11 years—attributed partly to BTS concert tourism. Analysts noted rising crude oil import costs at $112 per barrel could compress the annual current account outlook if the Strait of Hormuz closure persists.

stories.headline: US-China trade talks to be hosted on South Korean soil for first time
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce announced on May 10 that Vice Premier He Lifeng will lead a delegation to South Korea for trade negotiations with a US counterpart delegation on May 12-13, marking a significant diplomatic use of South Korean territory as neutral ground for the US-China trade dispute.

stories.headline: President Lee holds calls with Dutch and Canadian leaders on tech cooperation and trade
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung held phone calls with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten on May 7 and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also on May 7; with the Netherlands, Lee agreed to expand cooperation in semiconductors, AI, quantum technology, batteries, and offshore wind; with Carney, the conversation built on a recent Team Canada trade mission to Seoul, with Carney indicating he looked forward to hosting Lee for a visit. Coverage noted a South Korean submarine bid in Canada as a related item.

stories.headline: South Korea launches KRW stablecoin proof-of-concept and tightens overseas crypto transfer rules
stories.summary: South Korea passed legislation bringing offshore cryptocurrency transfers under foreign exchange regulations, while iM Bank partnered with BTQ Technologies and Finger to launch the country's first bank-led Korean won stablecoin proof-of-concept on the Kaia blockchain; separately, a PPP lawmaker criticized the National Tax Service for being underprepared to implement virtual asset taxation. A separate earlier initiative (TokenSquare/KRWQ with the BSV Association) also launched KRW stablecoin infrastructure.

stories.headline: Samsung exits China consumer electronics market, withdrawing all home appliance sales
